title: Hospital Operations Capacity Review
company: Harborview Hospital Analytics • Weekly Boss Case
context: The operations committee wants a synthetic capacity and waiting-time review. Use aggregate unit-day data only. Do not make diagnosis, treatment, or patient-level claims.
cleaningPrompt: Which controls are required before presenting the operations review? Select all required actions.
cleaningOptions: Validate arrivals, completed visits, waits and capacity fields are non-negative.
Check completed visits do not exceed arrivals and occupied beds do not exceed staffed beds where bed capacity applies.
Infer missing diagnoses from waiting time.
Treat every long wait as proof of poor clinical care.
cleaningExpectedSelections: Validate arrivals, completed visits, waits and capacity fields are non-negative.
Check completed visits do not exceed arrivals and occupied beds do not exceed staffed beds where bed capacity applies.
sqlPrompt: Using hospital_daily_ops, return unit and ROUND(AVG(avg_wait_minutes), 1) AS avg_wait_minutes grouped by unit.
kpiPrompt: Emergency average wait exceeded 60 minutes on 2 of 4 observed days. What percentage of observed Emergency days exceeded 60 minutes?
chartPrompt: Which visual best shows how waiting time changed across dates for each unit?
chartOptions: Line chart with date on the x-axis and one wait-time series per unit
Pie chart with each date as a slice
Scatter plot of unit names against text labels only
A gauge for every unit-day row
chartExpected: Line chart with date on the x-axis and one wait-time series per unit
recommendationOptions: Validate the high-wait pattern over more comparable weeks, investigate demand and capacity drivers, and test staffing or scheduling scenarios before operational rollout.
Change treatment protocols because wait time proves a clinical problem.
Use patient-level diagnosis assumptions even though the data is aggregate.
Ignore forecast capacity gaps because they are not actual arrivals yet.
recommendationExpected: Validate the high-wait pattern over more comparable weeks, investigate demand and capacity drivers, and test staffing or scheduling scenarios before operational rollout.
